Subject: Redwood Pricing Exhibit — redline and questions

Hi Hannah,

Attached is our redline of the pricing exhibit and a short set of questions from procurement. The two items that are blocking us are: (1) the discount phase-out language — we need a clear lookback period and confirmation that true-ups are applied monthly, and (2) the floor/cap language — the way it's written could trigger a material upsell charge mid-quarter if usage bursts.

We'd prefer a 90-day lookback for phase-out and a mechanism that limits retroactive reprice to invoice periods only. Can your team confirm these are negotiable?

Attachment: EnterpriseCo_pricing_redline_20250528.pdf (PDF, redlines + annotated comments)

Thanks,
Liam

Hi Liam — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're reviewing with Legal and Finance now. Quick notes:

- We think a 90-day lookback for the discount phase-out is reasonable from a commercial standpoint, but we need Legal to confirm the operational wording so billing doesn't need multi-period adjustments.
- On the cap/floor concern: our goal with the stabilization buffer was to avoid frequent churn on small bursts. Finance will run the billing workflow implications and Legal will propose language that limits retroactive charges to the invoice period.

Can we schedule a 30-min call Thursday to walk the proposed language? I'm free 10–12 ET. If that's tight, we can provide an edited exhibit first.

I'll follow up after Marissa and Karthik weigh in.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 May 2025 08:30:00 -0400
Subject: INTERNAL: redline notes — discount phaseout & cap/floor

Hannah / Karthik — see my annotated suggestions (attached). High-level position: we can accept a 90-day lookback but must limit the operational surface for billing to avoid perpetual true-ups. Suggested approach:

1) Discount phase-out: replace 'phase-out' paragraph with a two-sentence rule that defines (a) the lookback window (90 days) and (b) that any discount reduction is applied prospectively to the next invoice period; true-ups limited to a single invoice adjustment for the invoice period in which the trigger occurred.

2) Cap/floor (stabilization buffer): reword to a binding 'stabilization buffer' with a quantitative threshold (10% of average monthly usage over prior 90 days) before any upward reprice can be considered. If threshold exceeded, permitted remedy is a rate adjustment for the next billing cycle only — no retroactive multi-quarter recalculation.

3) Operational notes for Finance: add an explicit cross-ref to billing_workbook_v1.xlsx so accounts ops know which metric to use.

Attachment: marissa_redline_exhibit.docx (Word doc — legal redlines and substitute clauses)

If we're aligned, I'll draft the substitute language for Hannah to share externally. Also recommend offering a one-time credit cap (e.g., not to exceed $X) as a commercial sweetener to get to signature faster. Thoughts?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 15:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood Pricing Exhibit — redline and questions

Hi Liam — appreciate the patience while we reviewed internally. Attached is our proposed compromise and a short implementation note for Ops. Summary of the changes:

- 90-day lookback adopted; discount reductions will be applied prospectively to the next invoice period. Billing may make a single invoice-period adjustment if the trigger occurs within the invoice period, but we will not perform retroactive recalculations across multiple prior billing periods.
- Cap/floor replaced by a defined 'stabilization buffer' set at 10% of the trailing 90-day average. Only if usage exceeds that buffer will an upward rate adjustment be allowed, and that adjustment applies only to the next billing cycle.
- We're offering a one-time mitigation credit equal to the lesser of 1) $25,000 or 2) the computed incremental overage attributable to the triggering event, to be applied to the first adjusted invoice.

Next steps: if this is acceptable, we'll (1) update the order form and DocuSign package, (2) provide a short ops runbook referencing billing_workbook_v1.xlsx, and (3) loop in your procurement lead for signature. HubSpot deal link is included for reference.

Attachment: pricing_exhibit_response_20250530.pdf (PDF — proposed redline + ops note)
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/3492034/D-2025-0849

Proposed call: happy to take a 20-min call Monday AM if you'd like to talk through the changes.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
